::: {.why}
It is the most useful estimator in this half of the course and it is usually taught matrices first, which is backwards; the recursive weighted average is the idea and the algebra is bookkeeping.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- State what the filter does in one sentence containing no matrices, and say what the gain is a ratio of.
- Implement a scalar Kalman filter from scratch and show it reduces to a known estimator when the process noise is zero.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Work through chapters 4 and 5 of Kalman and Bayesian Filters in Python, the one-dimensional filter and the multivariate Gaussian chapters, running the notebooks rather than reading them.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Write your own twenty-line scalar filter with no library, and check two limits: with zero process noise it converges to the running mean, and with zero measurement noise it tracks the observation exactly. Those two checks are the whole intuition.
:::
:::
